On November 16, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to 
review the September Revenue versus Expenditure Report and various financial matters. The 
report, covering the first three months of Fiscal Year 2027, reflected revenues at 26% and 
expenditures at 37%, primarily due to the annual retirement system appropriation. The City and 
Springfield Public Schools finalized the net school spending carryover at $18,556,070. 
 
The committee reviewed several grants and financial items, including a donation to the senior 
center, a $1,000 Community Health Equity Survey grant, a $390,517 increase to the COPS Anti-
Heroin grant, a Municipal Road Safety grant, and a $58,500 Recycling Dividends Program grant. 
Additional items included SHINE program funding, $500,000 for the new East Springfield 
Library branch, federal funding for the Forest Park Horticulture and Learning Center, and cable 
access revenue allocated to FOCUS Springfield. The committee also reviewed the proposed 
transfer of $1 million from the Targeted Tax Relief Stabilization Fund to a special revenue 
account, a school roof replacement bond order, and the Fire Chiefs Association collective 
bargaining agreement covering 2024 through 2028. 
A motion was made to accept the committee items for further City Council consideration. The 
meeting adjourned at 5:11 p.m.
